title: Present Simple
theory:
## When do we use it?
Use the Present Simple to talk about habits, facts, schedules, and general truths — things that are always or usually true.

## How to form
With I / You / We / They → use the base verb.
With He / She / It → add -s (or -es / -ies).

### Spelling of the -s form
• Most verbs: add -s → work / works, eat / eats
• After -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -o: add -es → watch / watches, go / goes
• Consonant + y: change to -ies → study / studies, try / tries
• Irregular: have → has, do → does

## Negative & question
• Negative: I/You/We/They + don't + verb · He/She/It + doesn't + verb
• Question: Do / Does + subject + verb …?

## Examples
> I drink coffee every morning.
> She lives in Hanoi.
> The sun rises in the east.
> Do you play football? — Yes, I do.
> He doesn't eat meat.

## Common mistakes
• ❌ She go to school → ✅ She goes to school.
• ❌ He don't like rain → ✅ He doesn't like rain.
• ❌ I am play tennis → ✅ I play tennis.

title: Articles: a / an / the
theory:
## What is an article?
Articles are small words (a / an / the) used before a noun to say whether it is general or specific, known or unknown.

## a vs an
• Use a before a consonant SOUND: a book, a car, a university (sounds like "yu")
• Use an before a vowel SOUND: an apple, an hour (silent h), an honest answer

## the
Use the when both speaker and listener know exactly which thing is meant.
• Specific or already mentioned: I saw a dog. The dog was big.
• One-of-a-kind: the sun, the moon, the sky, the world
• Superlatives: the best, the largest
• Musical instruments: She plays the piano.

## No article
Use no article for general or uncountable nouns and for most names of people, cities, languages, meals.
• I love music. (in general)
• He speaks Vietnamese.
• We had dinner at 8.

## Examples
> I want an apple, please.
> She is a teacher.
> The book on the table is mine.
> Honesty is the best policy.

## Common mistakes
• ❌ She is teacher → ✅ She is a teacher.
• ❌ I love the music → ✅ I love music. (in general)
• ❌ An university → ✅ A university (sound starts with "yu").

title: Prepositions: in / on / at
theory:
## Quick rule of thumb
Think of size: at = a single point · on = a surface or line · in = inside something.

## For TIME
### at — clock times & specific moments
• at 7 PM, at noon, at midnight, at sunset
• at night, at the weekend (UK), at Christmas

### on — days & dates
• on Monday, on Friday morning
• on April 5, on my birthday

### in — months, years, seasons, parts of the day
• in January, in 2025, in summer
• in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening
• in a few minutes (future)

## For PLACE
### at — specific point or address
• at the door, at the bus stop, at home
• at school (= attending it), at work

### on — surfaces and lines
• on the table, on the wall, on the floor
• on the second floor, on the corner

### in — enclosed spaces / large areas
• in the box, in the room, in the car
• in Hanoi, in Vietnam, in the world

## Examples
> I'll see you on Monday at 9 AM.
> She was born in May 1998.
> The cat is in the box, on the chair, at the corner.

## Common mistakes
• ❌ In Monday → ✅ On Monday.
• ❌ At the morning → ✅ In the morning.
• ❌ On Hanoi → ✅ In Hanoi (cities use 'in').
